3. Omkar sits to the immediate left of the one who sits to the immediate left of Farida.
4. Only three persons sit between Dhruv and Kunal when counted from the right of Dhruv.
5. Only three persons sit between Uma and Pranav when counted from the left of Uma.
6. Only one person sits between Pranav and Varun when counted from the right of Pranav.
7. Varun sits to the immediate left of Omkar.
8. Uma is not an immediate neighbour of Lata.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits second to the right of Farida?

steps: Start with clues 1 and 4: together they fix Kunal, Wasim and Dhruv. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Clue 2 gives 4 cases — Case 1: Farida placed and Lata placed; Case 2: Farida placed and Lata placed; Case 3: Farida placed and Lata placed; Case 4: Farida placed and Lata placed.
Clue 3 cannot be met in Case 3, so it is rejected.
Clue 3 then places Omkar.
Clue 7 cannot be met in Case 1 and Case 4, so they are rejected.
Clues 7, 6 and 5 then place Varun, Pranav and Uma.
Harish takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from Kunal: Kunal, Pranav, Wasim, Lata, Dhruv, Harish, Farida, Uma, Omkar, Varun.
Farida faces the centre, so Farida's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Second to the right of Farida: Harish → Dhruv — answer **Dhruv**.

solution.trap: Omkar is second to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

options: U is an immediate neighbour of Q
T sits second to the right of S
T sits third to the left of Q

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 4, 8 and 7: together they fix L, P, V, S, N and R. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Clue 5 gives 2 cases — Case 1: T second to the left of P; Case 2: T second to the right of P.
Clue 3 splits Case 1 into 2 cases — Case 1a: M to the immediate left of L and U second to the right of L; Case 1b: M fourth to the left of L and U to the immediate left of L.
Clue 6 cannot be met in Case 1a and Case 2, so they are rejected.
Clue 6 then places Q.
Final arrangement, clockwise from P: P, M, T, V, S, Q, N, L, U, R.
(A) U is an immediate neighbour of Q — false.
(B) T sits second to the right of S — **true**.
(C) R sits exactly opposite Q — false.
(D) T sits third to the left of Q — false.
(E) Q sits exactly opposite R — false.
solution.shortcut: Test each statement on the final diagram, not on the clue list.
solution.trap: A statement copied from a clue with one word changed (left ↔ right, second ↔ third) looks familiar but is wrong.
